business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Multi-Axis Computerized Numerical Control Metal Centers

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Spain (Reino de España / Kingdom of Spain)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain – unitary national jurisdiction (no corporate sub-registry distinction; provincial Registros Mercantiles coordinated by the Registro Mercantil Central)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European), governed by the Código de Comercio (1885) and Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), with substantive EU-harmonized corporate and AML law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 6 Feb 1992; in force 12 Jan 1994, as amended 2005)
Spain–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 22 Nov 1990; amended by Protocol of 2 Apr 2011)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI), signed 30 Dec 2020 (ratification pending)
Spain–Latin America BIT and economic treaty network, including instruments with Mexico, Chile, Peru, Colombia and Argentina, supporting the stated Latin-America bridge strategy
EU–Chile Advanced Framework Agreement and EU–Mexico Global Agreement (Bridging EU-LATAM trade platforms)
ICSID Convention (Washington 1965) and UNCITRAL arbitration framework
Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (Spain and PRC both parties)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (AML/CFT), implemented by Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento), as amended; Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, and Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, creating and implementing the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (RCTR / central UBO register); Ley 58/2003 (General Tax Law, Arts. 8–9 on fiscal domicile); Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (dual-use export controls covering multi-axis CNC machine tools).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Restricted access post-CJEU joined cases C-37/20 & C-601/20 (22 Nov 2022): full access for competent authorities (SEPBLAC, AEAT, DGSJFP, judicial police, notaries), obliged entities performing customer due diligence, and natural or legal persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; general public open-access is materially curtailed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation / business license
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or equivalent foreign company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing state's designated authority (for PRC: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China, effective 7 Nov 2023) plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / current corporate register extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or Chamber of Commerce of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (for non-Hague states) plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passport / national ID of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) and each director-manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public competent at the place of residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification (compulsión), apostilled where required, followed by sworn translation into Spanish by a Traductor Jurado

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (Certificado de antecedentes penales) of the appointee director(s) and persons assuming significant management functions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Central de Penados (Ministerio de Justicia, Spain) or equivalent authority of the holder's state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct issuance in Spain, or Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation if issued abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence for the proposed equity contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature legalization of the bank officer via apostille (or notarization recognized by Spanish notarial practice) plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney to the incorporation agent / formation counsel (poder para la constitución)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the grantor's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states) and sworn Spanish translation; original protocol retained by the Spanish notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Compulsory pre-incorporation screening against (i) OFAC SDN/SSI consolidated list, (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP) as published in the Official Journal of the EU, (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List, and (iv) SEPBLAC/CNMV national risk lists; PEP status analysis (including second-degree family members and close associates) documented in the UBO questionnaire; enhanced due diligence under Ley 10/2010 Arts. 3 and 14–19 applied due to the High-Risk, Special-License AML tier, combined with mandatory dual-use end-user/end-use verification for five-axis CNC centers under Regulation (EU) 2021/821 Annex I (Cat. 2B001), requiring a certified End-User Certificate for each export shipment and SWIFT-wire/LC payment-path sanctions checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – online negative name certificate service operated by the Colegio de Registradores de España (www.rmc.es / www.registradores.org, 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate denomination must be expressed in Spanish (Castilian) script and characters; co-official regional languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician) are admitted but Latin-script only; foreign-language or non-Latin script denominations are not registrable. The name must end with 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; RMC rejects names phonetically identical or substantially similar to already registered names (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, Art. 408).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names incorporating public authority references (e.g., 'Ministerio', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Instituto Nacional', 'España', 'Comunidad Autónoma') – prior government authorization required

Reserved financial-sector tokens ('Banco', 'Caja', 'Aseguradora', 'Reaseguradora', 'Sociedad de Valores', 'Entidad de Pago', 'Capital-Riesgo', 'Fondo de Pensiones') – prior Banco de España / DGSFP authorization mandatory
Misleading, offensive, or contrary-to-public-order tokens under Art. 407 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; names suggesting a larger or foreign corporate group without actual group linkage
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative certificate expires 90 days from issue; it is non-extendable, and re-application requires a new fee and new submission. Up to five alternative denominations may be listed in priority order on a single application. On dismissal, the applicant may (i) opt for the next alternative name, or (ii) contest the RMC decision by filing an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes within one month of notification, per Ley 39/2015 (LPAC) Arts. 121–122, exhausting administrative remedies before contentious-administrative litigation before the Audiencia Nacional.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address can serve as a transitional administrative domicile but is NOT compliance-sufficient for ISIC 2822 CNC machining. The Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Art. 9) requires the registered seat to correspond to the actual place of management or principal operation. For the CNC five-axis activity, AEAT could re-assess tax residence, SEPBLAC expects a physical operational presence, and the municipal industrial license (licencia de apertura / comunicación de apertura) cannot attach to a virtual mailbox. The manufacturing plant must be the corporate address; virtual offices are acceptable only for a maximum one-month post-incorporation transitional period.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – estimated 45% to 55% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation, driven by AEAT stock/tax-domicile visits (Ley 58/2003 Art. 29), SEPBLAC AML no-notice visits, municipal industrial-license enforcement, and customs or state security forces dual-use audits on CNC inventory and end-user records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores de España
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registrars' statutory tariff (Real Decreto 1427/1989); EUR 15.00 per application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial public incorporation deed with by-laws (escritura de constitución y estatutos; capital EUR 3,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public (Ministerio de Justicia regulated notarial regime)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial arancel (Real Decreto 1426/1989) scaled to capital; market band EUR 380–500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for provisional tax ID (NIF provisional / CIF) upon execution of deed
Provisional NIF and deed docketing handling by authorized gestoría
Inscription of the S.L. in the provincial Registro Mercantil, including UBO (titularidad real) declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registrars' statutory tariff (Real Decreto 1427/1989); EUR 180.00 standard incorporation filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Capital transaction tax (ITP-AJD, modalidad operaciones societarias) on EUR 3,000 of capital – general regime 1%
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory rate 1% of nominal capital (regional exemptions may apply; Madrid 0%)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of six foreign corporate/UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in country of origin (PRC MFA; notarial dean's office in Spain)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or prevailing tariff of issuing authority; approx. EUR 10.00 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traducción jurada) of five foreign documents into Spanish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traductor Jurado appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; approx. EUR 40.00 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal advisory and AML compliance bundle: UBO piercing, PEP/OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, dual-use export-control readiness check (Regulation (EU) 2021/821), corporate by-law drafting review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border SL formation with high-risk AML tier; flat fee EUR 1,400

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July 2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Law (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 4 (minimum capital), 20 to 23 (incorporation deed and registration), 25 (registered office) and 58 (appointment of directors); supplemented by Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Commercial Registry Regulations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for the negative name certificate; Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the province of the registered office for the obligatory inscription of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public incorporation deed (Escritura Pública de Constitución) granted before a Spanish notary, followed by registration (inscripción) in the Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum subscribed and fully paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 in cash, deposited with a Spanish credit institution in the name of the company in formation and confirmed by an irrevocable bank certificate (certificado bancario) annexed to the deed; the funds remain blocked until post-registration release. Capital contributions may not be deferred, and in-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], S.L. — Adopted by unanimous written consent of the founding shareholders on [DATE]. RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporation deed and annexed by-laws are approved in final form; (2) the entire subscribed capital of EUR 3,000 is confirmed fully subscribed and paid up under Article 4 of the Capital Companies Law; (3) the registered office is adopted at the address set forth in the deed; (4) the officers named are appointed under Article 58 and accept their offices; (5) the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, obtain the provisional NIF, pay incorporation taxes, and complete registration with the Mercantile Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Applying for the Negative Company-Name Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) through the Colegio de Registradores online portal or physical counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official name application (solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación) stating up to two preferred corporate names. The applicants' signatures must be notarized or authenticated before a notary or via secure electronic certificate. The certificate confirms that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or protected trade name and remains valid for three months, renewable once.
required_dossiers: Official name application form (solicitud de denominación social)
Notarized identification of the requesting founders or power of attorney
Proof of payment of the central registry fee
Copy of reserved/protected trade-mark certificates, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is denied due to name conflict or similarity, the applicants may submit alternate names, or file a gubernatorial appeal (recurso gubernativo) before the Directorate General of Legal Certainty within two months, presenting evidence of precedence or consent from the holder of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the Provisional Bank Account and Depositing Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution subject to Bank of Spain supervision and AML obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of 'the company in formation' (e.g., '[Company Name], S.L. en constitución'), deposit the fully paid-up minimum capital of EUR 3,000, and obtain a bank certificate (certificado bancario) identifying the depositors, the account holder and the amount. The notary will require this certificate at deed execution; funds are contractually blocked until presentation of the Mercantile Registry registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founding shareholder
Tax identification numbers (NIE/NIF) of the shareholders
Negative name certificate
AML/KYC forms and source-of-wealth declarations (sector classified as High_Risk_Special_License)
Draft by-laws or preliminary deed for account labelling
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or refuses the account, the founders may deposit with another authorized credit institution; the notary accepts any valid bank certificate, but a previously defective certificate must be replaced and an updated certificate submitted before deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Incorporation Deed Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary (notario) of the notarial district of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Grant the Escritura Pública de Constitución before the chosen notary, who verifies the legal capacity of the shareholders, the validity of the name certificate, the reality of the capital deposit, and the legality of the by-laws. The deed must contain the identity of each shareholder, the exact share allocation, the subscribed and paid capital, the form of administration, the registered office address, the corporate purpose (manufacture of multi-axis computerized numerical control metal centers) and the duration. The designated administrators accept their office in the same instrument.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate in force
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Passports and NIE/NIF of all founding shareholders
Draft incorporation deed and by-laws
Affidavit or certificate of non-resident tax identification for foreign shareholders
Declaration of no prior disqualification of the appointed directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses or notes defects, the founders execute a rectification deed (escritura de subsanación) or a new deed with corrected clauses; if the deposit certificate is irregular, the capital is re-deposited into a corrected account and a fresh certificate issued before notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Provisional NIF and Settling Transfer and Stamp Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) — provincial or online tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after executing the notarial deed, file Form 036 to register in the business census and obtain the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional). Simultaneously, self-assess the Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITPAJD) on capital allocation using Form 600 at the rate set by the autonomous community, ordinarily 1% of the stated capital. The provisional NIF is valid for up to six months and is later converted into the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Notarized first copy of the incorporation deed
Form 036 (census declaration)
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Modelo 600 ITPAJD self-assessment and payment receipt
Negative name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT rejects the provisional NIF application for formal defects, the applicant resubmits Form 036 with the certified copy of the deed and the missing attachments; if the ITPAJD assessment is queried, the payer may present a supplementary return within the statutory term before penalties accrue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Commercial Registry and Conversion to the Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office and the AEAT.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of notarial execution, file the first copy of the deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry, including all statutory annexes, via the electronic single window or the registrar's office. The registrar verifies the legality and capacity and, upon positive qualification, issues the registration certificate. With that certificate, the Company returns to AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF, and thereafter applies for the corporate seal, employer registration with the Social Security system, and the municipal activity license.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy of the incorporation deed
Negative name certificate
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Modelo 600 ITPAJD payment receipt
Form 036 with proof of AEAT filing
Certificates of no outstanding tax or social security liabilities, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect notice (calificación desfavorable), the notary or shareholders cure the defects by supplementary deed or document within the regression term; if the qualification is considered unfounded, an appeal (recurso gubernativo) may be filed with the Directorate General of Legal Certainty within two months from notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Tourism (Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo); the regional industry department of the autonomous community (Consejería de Industria); and the municipal authority (Ayuntamiento) exercising competence under Law 7/1985 on Local Government Bases for classified-activity licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal License for Classified Activity and Opening/Operation (Licencia de Actividad Clasificada y Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento) for an industrial machine-tool manufacturing establishment, or, where the autonomous community has deregulated the activity, a Sworn Declaration of Opening (Declaración Responsable de Apertura) accompanied by the corresponding technical certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico, MITECO) and the competent environmental authority of the autonomous community (Consejería de Medio Ambiente).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Simplified Environmental Impact Assessment (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada) under Annex II, Group 5 (metal-working and machining installations), of Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment; a full EIA is required if the facility falls under Annex I thresholds, and an Integrated Environmental Authorization (Autorización Ambiental Integrada) is mandatory if the installation exceeds the IPPC capacity thresholds of Law 5/2013 and Directive 2010/75/EU; small machining workshops may be limited to the municipal activity license plus environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Royal Decree 117/2003 on VOC solvent emissions (including solvent-consumption registers for installations exceeding 0.6 t/year and abatement obligations above 2 t/year); compliance with the BAT conclusions of Directive 2010/75/EU for ferrous-metal machining and cooling-water circuits; wastewater discharge limits under Royal Decree 817/2015 for discharges into public hydraulic domain and municipal sewerage by-laws for indirect discharges (pH, suspended solids, oil-grease and heavy-metal thresholds); hazardous waste management per Law 22/2011 and Royal Decree 180/2015 (waste-transfer identification documents) for machining oils, coolant emulsions, metal chips and scrap; and minimum noise and vibration attenuation levels under the local environment and noise ordinances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification of the industrial building and fire-fighting installations under Royal Decree 2267/2004 (Reglamento de seguridad contra incendios en establecimientos industriales); structural and load-resistance verification in accordance with the Technical Building Code (Código Técnico de la Edificación) and Eurocodes EN 1991 and EN 1993; workplace risk-prevention clearance under Law 31/1995 (Ley de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales), validated by the Labor Inspectorate (Inspección de Trabajo y Seguridad Social); and periodic inspection of electrical installations, pressure equipment, lifting machinery and ventilation systems by accredited control bodies (Organismos de Control), with the corresponding registration of the industrial establishment before the regional industry authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Spanish Tax Agency electronic headquarters (Sede electrónica de la AEAT) at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Corporate tax and VAT administration is national, subject to applicable regional special regimes, including the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF during incorporation and a definitive NIF from the AEAT. The incorporation deed, registry information, articles, identification of directors and shareholders, registered office, and beneficial ownership information are filed using Modelo 036, normally through a notary or authorized representative. The definitive NIF must be obtained after registration with the Mercantile Registry and the relevant registration details must be reported to the AEAT. A foreign entity conducting taxable activities in Spain generally obtains a Spanish NIF by filing Modelo 036 with the AEAT. The application requires evidence of legal existence, constitutional documents, registered address, tax residence, powers of attorney, identification of the legal representative, and, where applicable, Spanish NIEs. Foreign documents generally require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. VAT registration is made through Modelo 036; an EU VAT number and inclusion in the VIES system require the corresponding intra-Community operator registration. An EORI number is obtained through the AEAT for customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election. An SL is generally subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Available elections and regimes may include the consolidated tax group regime, the special regime for newly created entities, the regime for small entities where statutory conditions are met, the merger, demerger, contribution and exchange-of-securities regime, the Spanish holding-company participation exemption regime, and other special regimes under the Corporate Income Tax Law. Spanish transparent-entity treatment is limited and does not generally apply to an ordinary SL. Hybrid mismatch restrictions apply under the Corporate Income Tax Law and EU anti-tax-avoidance rules; they are statutory anti-abuse rules, not elective entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), administered under Law 37/1992 and implementing regulations. Customs duties and import VAT apply to imports. Intra-Community supplies and acquisitions are governed by EU VAT rules as implemented in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic VAT registration threshold applies to Spanish-established businesses: taxable persons must register before commencing taxable economic activities or making transactions requiring registration. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold may apply to qualifying intra-Community distance sales and certain cross-border B2C electronic services, subject to the Union OSS regime; it is not a general Spanish domestic VAT-registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal national real-time invoice-clearance mandate for all businesses. Taxpayers within the Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) regime, including generally businesses exceeding the EUR 6 million turnover threshold, VAT groups, and REDEME entities, must electronically transmit specified invoice-record data to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory exceptions. VAT invoices must satisfy Spanish electronic invoicing and integrity requirements. Law 18/2022 and Royal Decree 1007/2023 establish requirements for compliant invoicing software, including integrity, traceability, preservation, and anti-alteration controls, with implementation deadlines subject to subsequent regulatory changes. The broader private-sector B2B electronic invoicing mandate under the Create and Grow Law requires implementing regulations before full operation. Regional systems, such as TicketBAI, may apply in the Basque Country and are separate from the national framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spain to a destination outside the European Union may qualify as VAT-exempt with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the statutory exporter, transport, customs, and documentary conditions are satisfied. The exporter must retain the export customs declaration and reliable evidence of exit from the EU customs territory, together with the commercial invoice, transport documents, packing records, and proof linking the goods to the export transaction. Intra-Community supplies of goods are exempt with the right to deduct rather than technically zero-rated, generally requiring valid customer VAT identification, transport to another Member State, proper EC Sales List reporting, and evidence of cross-border transport. B2B services supplied to a non-Spanish business customer are generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rule, rather than exports subject to a 0% Spanish VAT rate. Special rules apply to services directly connected with exported goods, transport, intermediaries, and customs regimes. VAT refunds require valid invoices, accounting records, proof of payment where relevant, and evidence that input VAT relates to deductible business activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration, normally the export accompanying document or equivalent MRN-based customs evidence
Commercial invoice identifying exporter, consignee, goods, value, Incoterms, and destination
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or equivalent
Proof of exit from the European Union customs territory, such as customs exit results or equivalent electronic confirmation
EORI number and customs representation documentation where applicable
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification number, transport evidence, and EC Sales List reporting
Bank payment or other commercial evidence where relevant to substantiate the transaction and its consideration
Proof of importation or local delivery in the destination jurisdiction where reasonably available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general foreign-exchange repatriation requirement or universal 180-day deadline for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption or input VAT recovery may be denied or reversed where customs exit, transport, customer-status, invoice, accounting, or reporting evidence is incomplete or inconsistent. Recovered VAT may be assessed retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and applicable surcharges. VAT infringements may attract administrative penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly omitted or claimed amount, depending on the infringement, culpability, concealment, and aggravating factors; failure to issue or preserve invoices and accounting records may carry separate penalties. False customs declarations may trigger customs debt, import VAT, customs penalties, seizure, and loss of simplified procedures. Intentional tax fraud exceeding the applicable criminal threshold, generally EUR 120,000 of tax per tax period and tax, may constitute a criminal offense under the Spanish Criminal Code, with fines and possible imprisonment. Fraudulent export documentation can also result in denial of VAT refunds, joint-liability assessments, and enhanced audit review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acts as the national central bank and macro-supervisory authority; the foreign transactions and payments declaration regime is administered by the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores y Antiblanqueo de Capitales (DGTEA) within the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation (Ministerio de Asuntos Económicos y Transformación Digital). Banco de España also exercises prudential oversight over credit institutions under Law 10/2014 and the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) of the ECB.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area Member State; the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. The Spanish liberalization regime (Law 18/1992, Royal Decree 1816/1991 and Royal Decree 1006/2014, as amended) establishes an 'administrative liberalization' principle: no prior authorization is required for current account payments, foreign direct investment, loans, or profit repatriation. The only practical hurdles for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) are (i) the statutory 25% Corporate Income Tax (IS) on retained distributable earnings; (ii) the 19% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Treaty (e.g., China-Spain 1992, Mexico-Spain 1994, Chile-Spain 2004); and (iii) the Bank of Spain statistical reporting obligation for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 per operation or EUR 100,000 cumulative per calendar year. Capital injections and profit remittances are otherwise free of any exchange control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Spain. The obligation to surrender export proceeds to the banking system was abolished with the full liberalization of the Spanish foreign exchange regime in 1999 (entry into Economic and Monetary Union). An exporter may freely retain initial proceeds denominated in EUR or any foreign currency, hold them in domiciled accounts, or convert them at market rates. The only surviving obligations are (i) filing the Banco de España 'External Transactions Return' (declaración de operaciones con el exterior) under Royal Decree 1006/2014 for single transactions above EUR 50,000 or cumulative sums above EUR 100,000 per year; and (ii) maintaining underlying commercial documentation (invoices, transport documents, customs declarations) for audit and due diligence purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Capital Social) and Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account (preferably for treasury and wealth management, not the notarized capital escrow)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility for payment processing, but Low for statutory capital escrow. Spanish and EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed under Law 21/2010 and the EU EMD2 (2009/110/EC) may be passported into Spain and used for operational payments, trade disbursements, and FX conversion rails. Spain recognizes cross-border EMIs from the European Economic Area (e.g., companies authorized in Lithuania, Ireland, the Netherlands) without additional licensing. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not authorized to hold a notarized 'capital escrow' account because such an account requires a full credit institution under Law 10/2014 to issue the certificate of capital contribution (certificado de desembolso) that ranking of SL capital must be registered with the Mercantile Registry; (ii) UK-incorporated EMIs have lost EU passporting after Brexit and cannot operate in Spain under EEA passport rights; (iii) established Spanish clearing banks frequently 'de-risk' customers in high-risk industrial sectors, and EMIs are generally excluded from servicing capital account openings or end-user documentary LC operations. Feasibility rating: 7/10 for ancillary operational clearing engines, but the primary treasury structure must be grounded in a Tier-1 Spanish bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Spanish SL with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and a high-risk classification under ISIC 2822 (manufacture of multi-axis CNC metal centers, dual-use relevance), full remote onboarding is generally refused by Tier-1 Spanish banks. Banco de España Circular 3/2019 and the AML Law 10/2010 require complete UBO identification and enhanced due diligence. In practice: (i) at least one statutory director (administrador único/solidario) or a duly appointed financial attorney (apoderado) with a notarized general power of attorney granted in Spain must appear physically at the bank branch for the identity verification interview; (ii) this in-person mandate is absolute for opening the capital escrow account before the capital disbursement certificate can be notarized; (iii) remote video identification may be permitted only for operational accounts after the initial physical onboarding and only if the bank maintains an advanced e-ID verification mechanism; (iv) the corporate non-resident signatories could also be subject to bank-specific minimum presence requirements under the Fourth Anti-Money-Laundering Directive (EU 2015/849).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership situated in a high-risk third country or PEP status of the ultimate shareholders, or opaque corporate chain hiding the true owner of the Spanish SL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register chart (25%+ ownership), certified opening deed (Escritura de Constitución) with Spanish notary attestation, Registro Mercantil certificate of incorporation and current directors, passport/NIE copies of all natural-person UBOs, sworn bank references (issued within 3 months) from the investor's primary bank, audited financial statements of the parent entity, a structural shareholding explanatory memorandum, and, where applicable, a PEP risk declaration demonstrating legitimate source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use product exposure: CNC five-axis machining centers classified under EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 (Annex I Category 2B001) with potential military or proliferation end-uses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-User Certificate (EUC) or End-User Undertaking from the final customer for each export transaction, internal dual-use compliance manual (including ECCN and control status assessment, red-flag screening procedures, and restricted-end-use declarations), software/export control officer biography, the Spanish Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) dual-use authorization file number or a negative-control/non-tier memorandum, and historical transaction records demonstrating no prior adverse sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or unexplained cross-border capital inflow exceeding EUR 50,000 before full corporate registration, raising queries on Source of Funds (SoF) and Source of Wealth (SoW)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital increase agreement with prior risk of the Financing Act (Ampliación de Capital), notarized certificate of deposit (certificado de desembolso), bank statements from the remitting account showing clear provenance, sale-purchase contracts or investment agreements underpinning the funds, KYC questionnaires and a certified board resolution by the Spanish SL authorizing the treasury opening, plus a ForEx purpose code statement (Bank of Spain code I-3: Contributions to equity).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancies between projected trade volumes declared in ISIC 2822 business plan and actual treasury activity, or payment routing via non-bank, unlicensed providers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated business plan with realized order backlog (purchase orders, letters of intent), definitive supplier invoices and underlying logistics documents, existing supplier onboarding policy, a declaration of use for all current and intended clearing rails (SWIFT, MT103, LC), and a core treasury policy confirming that 100% of settlement flows will use licensed Spanish/EU credit institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity contributions must be routed as SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or SEPA CT for EUR payments from within the EEA. The Spanish SL's capital contribution should be preceded by a notarized deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) or a notarized capital increase resolution (Acuerdo de Aumento de Capital) for later registration. The wiring protocol requires: (i) beneficiary account number (IBAN) of the capital escrow account designated with the text 'Capital Social ES_SL'; (ii) the purpose code in the Remittance Information field must indicate 'Aportación de capital social' (equity increase) with the Spanish bank transaction type code A-3 (foreign investment in Spanish companies); (iii) the Bank of Spain statistical declaration (Declaración F3) must be filed when the amount exceeds EUR 50,000, or at the end of the calendar year when cumulative transactions exceed EUR 100,000; (iv) the remitting shareholder's bank must include the Spanish SL's NIF (CIF) in the supplementary/beneficiary information to avoid automatic AML blocking; and (v) banks require the notary's certificate or a draft deed reference number prior to releasing funds from the escrow account. Failure to maintain these purpose codes may result in forced returns or freezing of the inbound flow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments towards components, spindles, servo drives, castings and software licenses in the production chain of five-axis machining centers, the permissible clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers to supplier accounts (routine, for high-frequency low-value payments), with detailed invoice reference and Spanish bank purpose code for commercial imports (code C-1); (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 (ICC Uniform Customs and Practice) for large-ticket CNC main assembly or specialized extrusion purchases, including ICC eUCP for electronic presentation, with the LC purchase field stating the relevant HS codes and 'End-User Certificate' when dual-use regulation applies; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer Instant (SEPA CT Inst) or SEPA Business-to-Business (B2B) for intra-EEA settlement of suppliers within the European Union; and (iv) documentary collection (CAD / DA) is acceptable only if the underlying transaction volume remains below the EUR 100,000 individual reportable threshold. Any settlement above EUR 50,000 must be retained in the Banco de España reporting system, and disbursements for exported CNC two-five axis centers to Latin American buyers should be settled via an LC confirming bank in Spain to eliminate country transfer risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (deliverable) covered under EMIR and MiFID II (Ley 6/2023, de Mercado de Valores y Servicios de Inversión), executed under ISDA 2002 or a bank-form domestic master agreement.

Outright EUR/CNY deliverable forwards (CNH offshore market), permitted for trade operations with Chinese component suppliers; Spanish credit institutions treat the CNY/CNH spread as a driver and account for the non-deliverable alternative.
FX swaps (swap de divisas) for rolling short-term EUR/USD and EUR/CNY exposure, allowed under Spanish banking regulation and EMIR clearing thresholds, with standard T+2 or T+1 tenors.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between EUR and USD (or EUR and CNY) for longer-term maturity alignment of purchase finance and sale receivables, permissible under EMIR and the Securitization Law restrictions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for currencies with regulatory restrictions, such as the Chinese RMB when a full deliverable CNY route is unavailable; Spanish banks may offer CNH-enabled NDF-like structures, but they must comply with ESMA's product intervention rules and suit the Spanish SL's status as a non-financial counterparty (NFC-) under EMIR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) comprising the Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Statement of Changes in Equity, Cash Flow Statement, and Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) via the provincial Commercial Registry where the company's registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the company's fiscal year-end; filing due within one month after approval by the general meeting; standard 31 December fiscal year-end requires general meeting approval by 30 June and filing by 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines from €200 to €2,000 per irregularity, increased to €6,000 to €60,000 for repeated or late filings after enforcement notice; penalties for companies with annual turnover over €6 million may reach €12,000 per infraction; continued non-filing closes the company's tax registration and triggers closure of the commercial registry sheet, preventing lawful registered operations and leading to administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT - Spanish State Tax Administration Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end; for standard 31 December year-end, filing due by 1 July (or next business day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5% plus an additional 1% per month of delay up to 20%; late payment interest of 3.75% current statutory rate; penalties from 50% to 150% of the tax base where understatement is found; permanent blocking of tax certificate issuance until filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements in XBRL Format through the Electronic Filing System (Depósito de Cuentas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Colegio de Registradores de España via the Registro Mercantil Central electronic depository
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of annual accounts by the shareholders' meeting; accounts must be approved within six months of year-end, hence by 30 July for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine from €1,200 to €60,000, ranging from 0.05% to 1% of total assets; ineligibility to obtain the open registry certificate; administrative strike-off where deposit is not made for two consecutive fiscal years; closure of the registrar sheet under Article 378 of the Spanish Companies Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaración de Operaciones con Terceros (Form 347 Annual Transaction Report with Third Parties)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During February each year for transactions in the preceding calendar year; filing due by the last day of February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine from €150 to €20,000; for incorrect or incomplete data the fine is €300 per record or 1.5% of the associated amount if determinable; minimum total penalty €150; assessed interest on omitted related-party amounts; suspension of the VAT refund offset procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Certificate Renewal (Certificación Registro Mercantil) confirming updated corporate data and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually upon filing of the Annual Accounts; immediate issuance after validation of updated register entries; no separate anniversary renewal required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of evidentiary value and good standing presumption of registered corporate data; inability to obtain positive registry certificate for banking, credit, and cross-border commercial counterparty verification; administrative penalty for untruthful registered data

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Information Filing (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central through the company's registered agent; integrated with the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the Annual Accounts; due within one month after accounts approval and no later than 31 July for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine under the Spanish Companies Act and anti-money laundering regulations up to €60,000 for material omission; prohibition from registering other corporate deeds; potential criminal classification for false statements under Article 292 of the Spanish Penal Code

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where the entity meets at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive years: balance sheet total exceeds €2,850,000; annual net turnover exceeds €5,700,000; average headcount exceeds 50 employees. Smaller SL entities may also be required to audit where they hold special licenses, operate in the defense or regulated industrial sectors, or are parent companies of a group required to consolidate. Any entity presenting consolidated financial statements is always subject to audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP as codified in the Plan General de Contabilidad, approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007 and updated by Royal Decree 1/2021; fully aligned with IFRS as adopted by the EU for consolidated groups. IFRS-EU mandatory for consolidated financial statements of listed groups; non-consolidated Spanish SL entities apply the national Chart of Accounts except where EU Regulation 1606/2002 requires IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal owners and ultimate beneficial owners must be identified and registered every year at the time of filing the annual accounts. Where a share transfer has occurred during the year, the director must file a formal declaration of beneficial ownership (Declaración de Titularidad Real) with the Commercial Registry identifying each ultimate beneficial owner and the percentage of controlling interest. Individual ultimate beneficial owners holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of capital or voting rights must be declared; if no natural person holds such threshold, the declaration must state the absence and identify the senior management. The protocol requires the transfer book (Libro Registro de Socios) to be updated within one month of any transfer, and a notarized public deed for every inter vivos transfer of shares.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Consejeros o Administradores)
Share Transfer Record Book (Libro Registro de Transmisiones de Participaciones)
Accounting Books (Libros de Contabilidad) including Journal and Inventory-Accounts Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 to USD 2,500 per annum for a Spanish registered address, company secretarial services, and registered agent compliance support in Madrid or Barcelona
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 to USD 12,000 per annum for a statutory audit by a certified public auditor (auditor de cuentas) for a mid-size CNC machine tool manufacturer meeting the compulsory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat national corporate income tax rate for Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada under the Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (LIS), ordinary regime; newly created active SLs may apply a 15% rate to the tax base for the first two tax periods in which a positive tax base arises, excluding asset-holding companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for certain newly incorporated entities; R&D and innovation tax credits (deducciones por actividades de I+D+i) up to 15%-42% of qualifying expenses; accelerated depreciation and free amortization rights under the reduced-size entity threshold for CNC/machine-tool assets when annual net turnover is below EUR 10 million; no manufacturing-specific statutory tax holiday.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (Spanish LIS Art. 110 provides no fixed expiry period; annual compensation of the tax base may be limited depending on the taxpayer's net turnover, generally 50%-70% for certain large companies, with no time limit).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades; mandatory electronic filing through the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) Sede Electrónica using a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For an SL with a 31 December fiscal year-end, Modelo 200 must be submitted in the window from 1 July to 25 July of the following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal year-end, within the 25 calendar days immediately following six months after the tax period closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section: Resultado contable (Cuenta de Pérdidas y Ganancias)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter statutory accounting profit or loss determined under Spanish GAAP, including depreciation and amortisation of the CNC five-axis milling centers, inventories, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files on its own tax-resident personality; no apportionment of accounting profit to the foreign parent is permitted in the resident return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record permanent and temporary differences: transfer pricing adjustments, disallowed interest, tax amortisation reversals, revaluation reserves, and changes due to related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign shareholder is a related Latin American distributor, the transaction margin of the Spanish CNC manufacturer must be arm's length and documented in the Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section: Compensación de bases imponibles negativas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset previous tax loss carryforwards against the positive taxable base, respecting statutory annual offset thresholds and the indefinite carryforward rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards belong solely to the Spanish SL; they do not pass through to the non-resident shareholder and do not affect the foreign basis in the SL under Spanish law unless reorganisation rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section: Base imponible y cuota íntegra
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% general rate or the reduced 15% new-company rate to the adjusted taxable base to compute the gross tax charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends paid by the SL to a non-resident parent are not deducted from the taxable base; the gross tax charge is computed solely on Spanish-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only legally available deductions: R&D credits, export promotion credits if applicable, double-taxation relief, and withholding tax credits on Spanish-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' withholding on dividends is not credited in the corporate return; it is the shareholders' own tax to be relieved under DTA or Form 210.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a prior AEAT demand carries a surcharge of 5% of the tax due when filed within 3 months after the deadline, 10% from 3 to 6 months, 15% from 6 to 12 months, and 20% after more than 12 months, plus late-payment interest of 3.75% per annum; failure to file in whole can also trigger a minimum EUR 200 fine and administrative penalties of 50%-150% of any omitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% statutory withholding tax under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on dividends and profit-sharing distributions made by a Spanish SL to non-resident beneficial owners; no subnational or regional surcharge applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the country of residence covering the dividend payment date, provide it to the Spanish SL before the distribution date where possible, and complete the AEAT forms for non-resident withholding (Modelo 216 periodical declaration and Modelo 210 for refund/settlement). If the TRC is not available at payment time, the SL must withhold 19%; the non-resident may then file Modelo 210 within the four-year statute of limitations to claim the differential. For an EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, the parent must hold at least 5% of the SL's capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period and supply a residence certificate together with a written declaration of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR withholding on royalties and interest paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident is generally 19%. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, the rate is 0% for qualifying associated companies (25% direct shareholding or resident EU parent-sub/associate structure), subject to anti-abuse substance conditions. Under most Spanish double tax treaties, treaty withholding on industrial/commercial royalties is typically reduced to 10% and on interest similarly to 10%, though specific rates depend on the applicable treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR: The Spanish entity must prepare and retain a Local File when annual net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million, or when the total value of related-party transactions of a given category exceeds EUR 250,000; a Master File is additionally required when the consolidated group net turnover exceeds EUR 45 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Precio Libre Comparable / Comparable Uncontrolled Price)
Transactional Net Margin Method (Margen Neto Transaccional)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a codified Economic Substance Regulation similar to the UAE ESR; however, Spanish courts and the AEAT apply the general anti-abuse rule, substance-over-form doctrine, and the 'letter-box entity' doctrine under Arts. 15 and 13 LGT and Art. 34 General Tax Law. A CNC manufacturing SL must maintain a physical Spanish office, operational management, technical staff, Spanish bank accounts, local contracting, and actual decision-making functions; otherwise the tax administration may disregard the entity as an artificial structure and reallocate revenue to the true place of effective management or to the non-resident parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Intentional False Accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting Spanish-source revenue from the sale of CNC five-axis milling centers, issuing false invoices to an Ecuadorian or Latin American related importer, inflating deductible costs through bogus suppliers, or deliberately omitting income received via Swift wire transfers into an undisclosed Spanish or offshore bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the tax omitted, plus default interest at 3.75%; where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single tax year, the conduct is a criminal tax offence under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code punishable by 2 to 6 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under Art. 42.1 Ley General Tributaria if they were active participants in the concealment or allowed the entity to be dissolved without paying; in criminal cases directors face imprisonment, suspension from public subsidies and tax benefits, travel bans, and disqualification from acting as company administrators for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a Spanish SL with no physical industrial presence, no production facility, no warehouse or demonstrable personnel, and using the entity solely to route Latin American payments and commissions for CNC machine-tool sales without actual management functions in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT can ignore the intermediary entity and reattribute taxable income to the actual beneficial owner, disallow VAT input deductions, impose 50%-150% late-payment penalties, and publish the arrangement on the AEAT abusive tax scheme registry. The Spanish entity may additionally be fined under anti-money-laundering legislation for false economic purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and formal shareholders are personally liable for civil restitution where the entity is a mere facade; courts may 'pierce the corporate veil' for tax debts, impose director disqualification, and, if the shell entity operates as part of a criminal fraud network, impose prison sentences of 1 to 4 years for auxiliary tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Insufficient Documentary Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare the Local File/Master File for the Spanish CNC manufacturer, absence of an OECD-compliant benchmark showing arm's length gross margin, or pricing sales to the related Latin American distribution company at a systematic loss while foreign related parties retain profit in low-tax or no-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may perform a transfer-pricing adjustment increasing the Spanish taxable base; the related-party penalty is 15% of the amount of the adjustment if the taxpayer fails to apply a correct arm's length value, and failure to provide the required documentation leads to an additional fine equal to 2% of the total volume of related-party transactions in the tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign deficient transfer-pricing documentation or instruct the accountant to use an unreasonable margin can be jointly liable for the tax deficiency, and criminal liability for false documentation arises where the document is used to evade tax exceeding EUR 120,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, UBO and Cross-Border Wire Irregularities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Swift wire transfers for CNC machine-tool sales from jurisdictions considered high-risk, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the Spanish SL or the Latin American buyer, or transacting in a way structured unnecessarily in cash, cryptocurrency, or shell intermediary accounts to avoid banking scrutiny.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010 on Money Laundering, serious AML infringements are penalised up to EUR 150,000 per violation and very serious infringements up to EUR 600,000 or 5% of the value of the transaction, whichever is higher; a Spanish SL that is a manufacturer of dual-use precision machine tools may also face administrative suspension of the export license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who fail to adopt AML procedures are subject to personal civil fines and disqualification; where the wire structure conceals tax or sanctions evasion, directors may face imprisonment of 1 to 6 years for money laundering and personal seizure of corporate assets under veil-piercing rules.
